brief.headline: Memory rally accelerates on hyperscaler capex surge; Samsung HBM ramp mitigates SK Hynix share risk
brief.summary: <cite index="39-8,39-9">SK Hynix closed ~30% higher on July 31, marking its best day on record; Samsung closed ~27% higher</cite>, reversing extreme July selloff after <cite index="24-5">Amazon guided for $200B 2026 capex</cite> and <cite index="19-6">five hyperscalers plan $660-690B infrastructure spend in 2026</cite>. <cite index="15-9">DRAM contract prices projected to rise 58-63% QoQ in Q2 2026, NAND 70-75% QoQ</cite>, with <cite index="15-3">TrendForce expecting pronounced shortage through 2026</cite>. <cite index="52-13">Samsung passed Nvidia HBM3E 12-layer qualification in Sept 2025, reached volume shipments Oct 2025, with 2026 supply sold out</cite>; <cite index="53-3">HBM4 production scheduled for Feb 2026</cite>. <cite index="28-11">CoWoS supply-demand gap expected to narrow from ~20% to ~10% by end-2026</cite> as <cite index="35-1">TSMC CoWoS capacity reaches 120-130K wpm by end-2026, up from 13K at end-2023</cite>.
brief.pair_trade_view: Neutral-to-long Samsung vs. SK Hynix. Samsung's late-cycle HBM3E qualification (Sept 2025) and early HBM4 mass production timeline (Feb 2026) closes multi-year gap; 2026 HBM supply already sold out per filings. SK Hynix retains 50-57% HBM revenue share but faces Samsung pricing pressure as third qualified supplier. Both benefit equally from DRAM/NAND upcycle (58-75% QoQ contract price gains Q2 2026) and structural hyperscaler demand. Volatility extreme: 30% single-day moves signal repositioning risk, not fundamentals. Pair offers no edge; size both or neither.

memory_cycle.notes: Q2 2026 DRAM +58-63% QoQ, NAND +70-75% QoQ contract pricing per TrendForce. HBM supply sold out through 2027 across all three suppliers. Manufacturers reallocating capacity from PC/mobile to HBM/enterprise (3x wafer consumption vs. standard DRAM). Pricing power sustained by hyperscaler pre-commitments and capacity constraints; no meaningful relief until late-2027/2028 fab additions. ASP trajectory steeper than 2017-18 supercycle.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="9-3">SK Hynix controlled 57% global HBM revenue Q4 2025, Samsung 22%, Micron 21%</cite>. <cite index="5-6">HBM bit shipments projected to jump 35% in 2026 to 17.1B Gb</cite>. Samsung's qualification win breaks SK Hynix duopoly for Nvidia supply but <cite index="51-5">near-term Samsung shipment volumes limited as third supplier</cite>. <cite index="5-7">SK Hynix expects minimal-to-modest HBM3E price downtick 2026 vs. 2025</cite> despite Samsung entry. <cite index="8-4">Top three makers allocated full HBM output for year, Micron guiding 68% gross margin Q2 2026</cite>. HBM4 race: Samsung targeting Feb 2026 mass production; SK Hynix completed development but timeline unclear. Watch for Samsung discounting to gain share.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix post record single-day gains on hyperscaler capex revival
news_pulse.implication: Violent reversal after July capitulation; SK Hynix +30%, Samsung +27% on July 31 following Amazon $200B capex guide and Microsoft/Meta AI spending affirmation. Short-covering and foreign inflows driving snapback. Positioning had turned extremely bearish; fundamentals (HBM sold out, DRAM +60% QoQ) unchanged.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscalers commit $660-690B capex for 2026, up 81% YoY
news_pulse.implication: Amazon $200B, Alphabet $175-185B, Meta $115-135B, Microsoft $120B+, Oracle $50B. ~75% allocated to AI infrastructure (GPUs, HBM servers, networking). All hyperscalers report supply-constrained, not demand-constrained. Direct upside for memory ASPs and bit demand through 2027.

news_pulse.headline: DRAM contract prices to rise 58-63% QoQ Q2 2026, NAND 70-75%
news_pulse.implication: Following Q1 DRAM +90-95% QoQ. NAND acceleration outpacing DRAM for first time this cycle. Suppliers reallocating to enterprise SSDs and HBM; PC OEMs receiving lower allocation, forced to pay spot premiums. Cloud providers committing multi-quarter purchase agreements. Shortage extends through 2026.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung passes Nvidia HBM3E qualification, 2026 supply sold out
news_pulse.implication: Qualification achieved Sept 2025 after 18-month delay; volume shipments began Q3 2025. HBM4 samples shipped to Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Google; preorders for 2026 HBM exceed planned output. Breaks SK Hynix exclusive Nvidia supply for Blackwell/Rubin. Risk: Samsung may discount to gain share, pressuring industry ASPs.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS capacity to hit 120-130K wpm by end-2026, gap narrows to 10%
news_pulse.implication: 10x expansion from 13K wpm end-2023. Supply-demand gap narrows from 20% to 10% by end-2026; further improvement 2027. Nvidia secures 60% of total capacity. Eases HBM-to-logic integration bottleneck for AI accelerators; positive for memory attach rates and hyperscaler deployment velocity.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix maintains ~50% HBM market share in 2026 despite Samsung entry
news_pulse.implication: UBS channel checks indicate SK Hynix holds stable ~50% bit share 2026. Pricing pushback risk as Samsung ramps but SK Hynix expects minimal-to-modest downtick. First-mover advantage (HBM3E March 2024) and Nvidia/hyperscaler pre-commitments protect share. Samsung's 2026 ramp incremental, not substitutive.

news_pulse.headline: Memory makers guided 68% gross margin Q2 2026 on HBM/enterprise mix
news_pulse.implication: Micron guiding 68% GM Q2 2026; HBM3E consumes 3x wafer area vs. standard DRAM. Full HBM output pre-sold for year across Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron. Margin gap explains continued PC/smartphone memory deprioritization. Structural profitability step-change if HBM demand sustains through 2027-28.

news_pulse.headline: AI capex-to-revenue gap widens to 46%, exceeds 2001 telecom divergence
news_pulse.implication: Sequoia calculates ~$600B annual revenue gap between hyperscaler AI capex and ecosystem sales; gap widening in 2026. Allianz pegs divergence at 46% vs. 32% in 2001 telecom bubble. Near-term risk: capex fatigue, credit spread widening (Oracle CDS tripled since Sept). Memory benefits from spend but watch hyperscaler FCF and debt issuance.

brief.derivatives_signal: No liquid equity derivatives for 005930.KS / 000660.KS; ADRs (SSNLF, HXSCL) thinly traded OTC. KOSPI 200 futures volatility elevated post-circuit breaker events July 29-30. Institutional commentary (Fibonacci Asset Mgmt) flags extreme positioning unwind and short-covering driving July 31 rally; expect continued volatility. Monitor SOXX (iShares Semiconductor ETF) for global sentiment; +8% July 30 catalyzed Korea rally. No actionable derivatives edge on Korea names; use cash equities or SOXX exposure.
